scenes.tts: How can one cut at a membrane send one signal inward while keeping another at the surface? Follow a single plasma membrane closely around one cell. The answer depends on where each product can go after the cut.
scenes.caption: How can one cut at a membrane send one signal inward while keeping another at the surface? Follow a single plasma membrane closely around one cell. The answer depends on where each product can go after the cut.
scenes.visual: 16:9 schematic cell cross-section, carried through the entire film. COLOR MAP for both films: PIP2 GOLD; IP3 BLUE; DAG ORANGE; calcium GREEN; PLC WHITE; conventional PKC TEAL; Gq route PURPLE; receptor-tyrosine-kinase route MAGENTA. A thick plasma-membrane band spans the upper third and an ER sac curves across the lower third. A GOLD labelled block, 'PIP2', sits in the inner leaflet. Slow lipid drift and ER shimmer continue. On the question, the PIP2 block pulses and a WHITE question mark divides into one arrow toward the ER and one arrow along the membrane. Keep a small 'schematic' label at bottom right.
scenes.narration: How can one cut at a membrane send one signal inward while keeping another at the surface? Follow a single plasma membrane closely around one cell. The answer depends on where each product can go after the cut.

scenes.visual: Over the moving cell world, title 'One Cut, Two Destinations' fades in for two seconds. The gold PIP2 block and both question arrows remain visible and gently move.

scenes.tts: The starting block is P I P two, a lipid in the inner leaflet of the plasma membrane. Its oily tails stay buried, while its charged head faces the watery cytosol. The same lipid serves as an address label and a stored signal. Phospholipase C approaches from inside the cell.
scenes.caption: The starting block is PIP2, a lipid in the inner leaflet of the plasma membrane. Its oily tails stay buried, while its charged head faces the watery cytosol. The same lipid serves as an address label and a stored signal. Phospholipase C approaches from inside the cell.
scenes.visual: Zoom until the membrane fills most of the frame height. The GOLD PIP2 block becomes a simple two-part cartoon: a small head block above two short tail bars, with no atoms or bonds. Label the halves 'charged head' and 'oily tails'. The head bobs in the cytosol while the tails sway inside the membrane. A WHITE rounded block labelled 'PLC' glides toward the junction between head and tails.
scenes.narration: The starting block is PIP2, a lipid in the inner leaflet of the plasma membrane. Its oily tails stay buried, while its charged head faces the watery cytosol. The same lipid serves as an address label and a stored signal. Phospholipase C approaches from inside the cell.

scenes.tts: The enzyme cuts between the head and the glycerol carrying the tails. Both products begin at the same tiny patch of membrane. Which product can leave the bilayer? Choose the phosphate-rich head or the oily pair of tails.
scenes.caption: The enzyme cuts between the head and the glycerol carrying the tails. Both products begin at the same tiny patch of membrane. Which product can leave the bilayer? Choose the phosphate-rich head or the oily pair of tails.
scenes.visual: PLC closes like a plain clamp across the join, without showing chemical structure. A bright cut line flashes. The separated head is labelled 'IP3' in BLUE and the tail block 'DAG' in ORANGE, but both remain held at the membrane. A question appears above: 'Which product leaves?' The BLUE and ORANGE blocks pulse alternately.
scenes.narration: The enzyme cuts between the head and the glycerol carrying the tails. Both products begin at the same tiny patch of membrane. Which product can leave the bilayer? Choose the phosphate-rich head or the oily pair of tails.

scenes.visual: Deliberate predict pause. Hold 'Which product leaves?' The BLUE IP3 and ORANGE DAG blocks bob gently in place; membrane lipids drift and the ER shimmers. Nothing reveals the answer.

scenes.tts: I P three carries three phosphates, so it dissolves in cytosol and moves away. D A G keeps two oily tails, so it stays in the inner leaflet. Their different chemistry creates a moving branch and a local membrane branch. One cut has created two second messengers in different places.
scenes.caption: IP3 carries three phosphates, so it dissolves in cytosol and moves away. DAG keeps two oily tails, so it stays in the inner leaflet. Their different chemistry creates a moving branch and a local membrane branch. One cut has created two second messengers in different places.
scenes.visual: The question fades. The BLUE IP3 block releases from the membrane and drifts down a curved path toward the ER. The ORANGE DAG block settles sideways into the membrane and begins a slow local oscillation. Labels 'water-soluble' and 'membrane-retained' travel with them. A bracket joins both labels under 'two second messengers'.
scenes.narration: IP3 carries three phosphates, so it dissolves in cytosol and moves away. DAG keeps two oily tails, so it stays in the inner leaflet. Their different chemistry creates a moving branch and a local membrane branch. One cut has created two second messengers in different places.

scenes.tts: Different receptors can start the same cut. A G protein coupled receptor activates G q, which activates P L C beta. A receptor tyrosine kinase displays phosphorylated tyrosines, where S H two domains dock P L C gamma. Docking places P L C gamma beside the receptor kinase. The kinase phosphorylates it and releases its internal brake. Both enzymes then make the same cut, producing I P three and D A G.
scenes.caption: Different receptors can start the same cut. A G-protein-coupled receptor activates Gq, which activates PLC-beta. A receptor tyrosine kinase displays phosphorylated tyrosines, where SH2 domains dock PLC-gamma. Docking places PLC-gamma beside the receptor kinase. The kinase phosphorylates it and releases its internal brake. Both enzymes then make the same cut, producing IP3 and DAG.
scenes.visual: Pull back to the full cell. On the left, a PURPLE seven-pass receptor block activates a PURPLE 'Gq' circle, which carries a WHITE 'PLC-beta' block toward one gold PIP2. On the right, two MAGENTA receptor blocks meet; small phosphate badges appear on their cytosolic tails. A WHITE 'PLC-gamma' block with two labelled 'SH2' grips docks there, with a small grey 'brake' block covering its cutting face. Docking alone does NOT cut: hold PLC-gamma docked and idle for a beat. Then, on 'phosphorylates it', a phosphate badge jumps from the receptor onto PLC-gamma, the brake block swings aside, and only then does PLC-gamma cut its PIP2. On 'Both enzymes then make the same cut', both cuts release a BLUE IP3 and leave an ORANGE DAG.
scenes.narration: Different receptors can start the same cut. A G-protein-coupled receptor activates Gq, which activates PLC-beta. A receptor tyrosine kinase displays phosphorylated tyrosines, where SH2 domains dock PLC-gamma. Docking places PLC-gamma beside the receptor kinase. The kinase phosphorylates it and releases its internal brake. Both enzymes then make the same cut, producing IP3 and DAG.

scenes.tts: Now follow I P three. It crosses the cytosol and binds an I P three receptor in the endoplasmic reticulum. That receptor is a calcium channel. I P three does not carry calcium; it opens the route out. The channel opens, and green calcium dots flow from the store into cytosol.
scenes.caption: Now follow IP3. It crosses the cytosol and binds an IP3 receptor in the endoplasmic reticulum. That receptor is a calcium channel. IP3 does not carry calcium; it opens the route out. The channel opens, and green calcium dots flow from the store into cytosol.
scenes.visual: Camera follows one BLUE IP3 block to the ER. A large channel gate labelled 'IP3 receptor' fills the centre. The blue block settles into a labelled socket; the gate swings open. GREEN calcium dots, initially dense inside the ER and sparse outside, stream through and spread upward. The ORANGE DAG block remains visible in a small membrane inset at top.
scenes.narration: Now follow IP3. It crosses the cytosol and binds an IP3 receptor in the endoplasmic reticulum. That receptor is a calcium channel. IP3 does not carry calcium; it opens the route out. The channel opens, and green calcium dots flow from the store into cytosol.

scenes.tts: Researchers tested whether I P three was sufficient without a hormone. They made a cell surface leaky while internal stores stayed sealed. No outside hormone was present. Added I P three released calcium from a nonmitochondrial store. That separation of cause from hormone made I P three a true messenger. Later work identified the store as endoplasmic reticulum.
scenes.caption: Researchers tested whether IP3 was sufficient without a hormone. They made a cell surface leaky while internal stores stayed sealed. No outside hormone was present. Added IP3 released calcium from a nonmitochondrial store. That separation of cause from hormone made IP3 a true messenger. Later work identified the store as endoplasmic reticulum.
scenes.visual: Transform the cell outline into a labelled 'permeabilized cell' with several small openings in only the plasma membrane. An internal store labelled 'internal store' and a separate grey mitochondrion remain sealed. A BLUE IP3 block enters through a surface opening; no receptor or hormone appears. GREEN calcium exits the internal store while the mitochondrion remains unchanged. A result label appears: 'IP3 sufficient for release'. Only on the final sentence, add the label 'ER' to the store.
scenes.narration: Researchers tested whether IP3 was sufficient without a hormone. They made a cell surface leaky while internal stores stayed sealed. No outside hormone was present. Added IP3 released calcium from a nonmitochondrial store. That separation of cause from hormone made IP3 a true messenger. Later work identified the store as endoplasmic reticulum.

scenes.tts: Return to the original cell. The moving branch is I P three, which opens the calcium channel. The local branch is D A G, still marking the membrane. Keep this rule. One P I P two cut sends I P three away. It leaves D A G at the membrane.
scenes.caption: Return to the original cell. The moving branch is IP3, which opens the calcium channel. The local branch is DAG, still marking the membrane. Keep this rule: one PIP2 cut sends IP3 away and leaves DAG at the membrane.
scenes.visual: Restore the carried cell cross-section. The BLUE route from plasma membrane to ER and the GREEN calcium plume glow together under label 'mobile branch'. The ORANGE DAG block pulses at the plasma membrane under label 'local branch'. Both routes then trace back to one GOLD PIP2 cut. The colour map stays visible as a compact legend for the second film.
scenes.narration: Return to the original cell. The moving branch is IP3, which opens the calcium channel. The local branch is DAG, still marking the membrane. Keep this rule: one PIP2 cut sends IP3 away and leaves DAG at the membrane.

scenes.visual: Dim the same moving cell world. Show one centred line only, exactly: 'One PIP2 cut sends IP3 away and leaves DAG at the membrane.' BLUE IP3 continues drifting toward the ER while ORANGE DAG sways in the plasma membrane.
